# Delivery position
## Departures

> Runway **04R/22L** is used for **departures**.
{.is-info}

All departures must climb to **FL100**, _except_ in the following 2 cases:

- **Northbound departures** are cleared to **FL130** (PERUS, BODRU, BADOD, OKTET and IRMAR)
- **Turboprop-equipped aircraft** must be cleared to **FL70 on #B departures**. These departures do not exist for Northbound departures, where the previous rule applies.

> All initial levels are published on the charts. However, in the context of VATSIM, **best practice is to systematically issue the initial level** clearance in order to avoid any surprises.
{.is-info}

## Special cases

At Nice, all departures are RNAV 1 (including published omnidirectional departures); for traffic unable to follow an RNAV 1 procedure[1], an omnidirectional departure followed by radar vectoring must be coordinated with Departure and Tower. In most cases, this will be similar to the missed approach procedure[2] in use.

There are RFL[3] restrictions for traffic bound for Geneva (LSGG), Zurich (LSZH), and airports in Corsica.

```diagram

```

For IRMAR, BADOD and OKTET only (requires Approach's agreement):

- #C departures: aircraft with a low initial climb rate, upon crew request (QFU 043)
- #Z departures: aircraft with a low initial climb rate, upon crew request (QFU 223)
- IRMAR #P: QFU 223 only, very high-performance aircraft, upon crew request.

## During events

To limit the amount of traffic on the GND frequency (due to the impossibility of splitting this frequency), best practice is to keep aircraft on the DEL frequency until they are ready to push back.

As on all airports, the use of PDC is recommended.


[1] RNAV1: See 22.4.2.2 et 22.4.3 in French AIP
[2] MAP: Missed Approach Procedure
[3] RFL : Requested Flight Level
